## Why visit

A beer experience that remains distinctive even after many European pub trips: the seating occupies former police cells, with heavy doors and a compact courtyard behind the enclosing walls. The novelty is supported by a serious cask selection rather than being the only reason to come. Pick a cell for a leisurely drink and notice the building’s scale and surviving features. It fits especially well between the waterfront and Ropewalks, and makes a useful different kind of historic stop after Liverpool’s ornate brewery-built interiors.

## Food

No kitchen. The official site permits takeaway food from neighbouring Amalia; confirm this remains acceptable on the day.

## Plan the visit

Cells are seating areas, not a booked museum tour. Sports and events can affect atmosphere; check before expecting quiet.

**Getting there:** Near Liverpool ONE and the waterfront; Liverpool Central is the nearby rail option.
